leotard.definition: A close-fitting garment worn for dance or gymnastics.

tights.definition: Skintight knit hose covering the body from the waist to the feet worn by acrobats and dancers and as stockings by women and girls.

ballet-shoes.definition: Soft lightweight shoes designed for ballet practice and performance.
ballet-shoes.exampleUsage: The dancer changed into ballet shoes before class.

jazz-shoes.definition: Flexible close-fitting shoes designed for jazz dance and similar studio movement.
jazz-shoes.exampleUsage: The jazz shoes had flexible soles.

tap-shoes.definition: Dance shoes fitted with metal plates that create rhythmic sounds when they strike the floor.
tap-shoes.exampleUsage: The tap shoes made clear sounds on the studio floor.

tutu.definition: Very short skirt worn by ballerinas.

leg-warmers.definition: Knitted or stretchy coverings worn over the lower legs for warmth during dance or exercise.
leg-warmers.exampleUsage: The dancer wore leg warmers during the warm-up.

headband.definition: A band worn around or over the head.

dance-belt.definition: A supportive undergarment worn by some male dancers beneath close-fitting dancewear.
dance-belt.exampleUsage: The costume guide lists a dance belt as specialized performance clothing.

skirt.definition: Cloth covering that forms the part of a garment below the waist.

dance-floor.definition: A floor surface intended for dance practice or performance.
dance-floor.exampleUsage: The studio's dance floor is kept clean and clear.

wall-mirror.definition: A large mirror fixed to a wall, often used in studios to observe movement and alignment.
wall-mirror.exampleUsage: Dancers could see the group in the wall mirror.

barre.definition: A bar dancers hold for balance while they warm up, practice, and stretch.

sound-system.definition: A group of electronic devices plays recorded sound or increases its volume throughout a particular room, hall, or vehicle.
sound-system.exampleUsage: The sound system was used during the activity.

changing-room.definition: A private room where people change clothes.
changing-room.exampleUsage: Students changed into dancewear in the changing room.

water-fountain.definition: A public device that supplies drinking water.
water-fountain.exampleUsage: The water fountain was used during the activity.

dance-bag.definition: A bag used to carry dance clothing, shoes, and accessories.
dance-bag.exampleUsage: Her dance bag contained shoes and a water bottle.

towel.definition: A piece of absorbent cloth used for drying your body or other things.

rosin-box.definition: A container holding powdered or solid rosin used in some dance settings to increase shoe grip where permitted.
rosin-box.exampleUsage: The studio controls use of the rosin box to protect the floor.

ballet.definition: A formal style of dance using precise movements and body positions.

pointe-shoes.definition: Special reinforced ballet shoes designed for trained dancers performing pointe technique under qualified instruction.
pointe-shoes.exampleUsage: Pointe shoes are used only after appropriate training and teacher approval.

bun.definition: A hairstyle with the hair gathered into a rounded shape.

arabesque.definition: Position in which the dancer has one leg raised behind and arms outstretched in a conventional pose.

pli.definition: A ballet movement in which the knees bend while the body remains controlled and aligned.
pli.exampleUsage: The teacher demonstrated a plié during the beginner class.

pirouette.definition: (ballet) a rapid spin of the body (especially on the toes as in ballet).

jet.definition: A quick leap or jump in dance, especially a large traveling jump.

pas-de-deux.definition: A ballet duet for two dancers, typically a ballerina and a male dancer in a leading role.

relev.definition: A ballet movement in which the dancer rises onto the balls of the feet or, for trained pointe dancers, onto the toes.
relev.exampleUsage: The class practiced a basic relevé under the teacher's supervision.

jazz.definition: A dance style using rhythmic, expressive movements and influences from jazz music.

tap.definition: A small metal plate that attaches to the toe or heel of a shoe (as in tap dancing).

hip-hop.definition: A style of dance associated with hip-hop music and culture.

ballroom.definition: Partner dancing, often including formal styles such as the waltz.

latin.definition: Dance styles with Latin American influences, such as salsa and rumba.

folk-dance.definition: A traditional dance from a particular community or region.

breakdancing.definition: An athletic street-dance style involving rhythmic footwork, freezes, and other movements, also called breaking.
breakdancing.exampleUsage: The supervised class introduced basic breakdancing history and movement vocabulary.

swing.definition: A lively partner dance style developed alongside swing music.

waltz.definition: A ballroom dance in triple time with a strong accent on the first beat.

stretch.definition: A large and unbroken expanse or distance.

spin.definition: To turn around quickly on one spot.

leap.definition: To jump through the air, often moving forward.

turn.definition: The act of changing or reversing the direction of the course.

kick.definition: To strike or push something with a foot.

step.definition: A sequence of foot movements that make up a particular dance.

slide.definition: A smooth surface children slide down for fun.

bend.definition: To cause (an object) to assume a crooked or angular form.

twist.definition: To cause (an object) to assume a crooked or angular form.

balance.definition: Harmonious arrangement or relation of parts or elements within a whole (as in a design).

choreographer.definition: A person who creates new dances.

dance-teacher.definition: A person who teaches dance technique, movement, choreography, or performance skills.
dance-teacher.exampleUsage: The dance teacher led the warm-up.

partner.definition: The person with whom someone performs a paired dance.

soloist.definition: A dancer performing alone or taking a featured individual role.

ensemble.definition: A group of dancers who perform together.

understudy.definition: To be an understudy or alternate for a role.

judge.definition: An official who evaluates performances in a dance competition.

dj.definition: A person who announces and plays popular recorded music.

salsa.definition: A lively partner dance with Latin American roots and rhythmic steps.

breakdance.definition: To perform breaking, an athletic street-dance style.
breakdance.exampleUsage: The students learned about how performers breakdance in a supervised class.

mat.definition: A thick flat pad used as a floor covering.

pointe-shoe.definition: A single reinforced ballet shoe designed for trained pointe work under qualified instruction.
pointe-shoe.exampleUsage: The pointe shoe was professionally fitted.

leg-warmer.definition: A knitted or stretchy covering worn over one lower leg for warmth.
leg-warmer.exampleUsage: The dancer wore a leg warmer during rehearsal.

bow.definition: Front part of a vessel or aircraft.
